Interviewing Steven Pinker on AGI, x-risk, and AI consciousness. Steven laid out why he's unfazed by instrumental convergence, why he's sceptical about AI consciousness, and what concrete events would change his mind about both!
I got insulted online by Scott Alexander!   Fun times.    I guess he hasn't read any of my work since the 1980s. https://t.co/KmciJm7gjx https://t.co/JwlKYdZS9l
@MelMitchell1 I didn't mean for that to be an insult, but feel free to link me to your relevant work and I will read it as penance.

@slatestarcodex Check out my Google Scholar page.   I've done many things since my PhD work in the 1980s on analogy (which actually did work out in its limited domain) and have done a lot of research on "modern LLMs".  E.g., my most recent two papers, both accepted at NeurIPS 2027.
@slatestarcodex Also nice to hear that reading my work is seen as "penance".

@MelMitchell1 I'll take a look. I didn't mean to belittle you, I just don't think it's right to cite you as one of the three experts representing a consensus on whether AI can be dangerous, in an article claiming that "scientists" rejected this conclusion.

@slatestarcodex 1. I believe that AI can be dangerous (& already is).  2. I am skeptical of claims that AI could cause human extinction.  3. I had no involvement in the article you cite.  4. AI field is polarized, but it's not helpful to (yes) belittle expertise of people you disagree with.

Sorry, but I stand by this. I am generally all in favor of truth-seeking ... when someone spreads misinformation about you, then you have to respond by saying, clearly, that you think their conduct is unacceptable. ... I just don't think it's stable to keep pretending that everything is fine after someone repeatedly knives you. ...

Scott Alexander has replied to Steven Pinker. He makes some good point as you'd expect, especially on the capability of the models. I was less convinced when he tried to explain why LLMs would become power seeking. He also calls me a 'culture warrior' & 'lowest quality voice' in the debate.  https://t.co/cG1NvnCwEd

This sentence from Scott's post is pure millenarianism. I have an article coming out tomorrow in @thedispatch about why the AI Faith, including @AnthropicAI is a new millennium cult. Somewhat surprised to see it encapsulated so clearly here. https://t.co/winFFeEiWI

@thedispatch @AnthropicAI This paragraph is particularly strange. I don't do on camera debates & have never been screamed at & never invited nor demanded that Scott have a debate with me. Bizarre. https://t.co/pq8Iv00l1h
Where I have "viciously smeared" Scott Alexander? https://t.co/hDAFgkdFrO

@ciphergoth @NathanpmYoung As I said in my original tweet, Scott makes good & important points, (including about me) but anyone who doesn't already agree with him substantively is going to be put off by the aggression in the piece. Particularly given that Steve was so generous in his own essay.

Do you mean misinformation about Scott in particular, or the rationalist/AI Safety community? Because it's one thing to argue that position X is wrong, quite another to describe position X as "being knifed." (If Pinker had spread some defamatory material about Scott, I would understand the response, but I do not think he has done that.)

Scott, its dishonest to argue that I wrote that the 'scientific consensus is that AI is not dangerous.' You're referring to a headline (which I did not write), and are omitting the fact that I did cite people like @GaryMarcus who point out catastrophic risk. https://t.co/1xrntmv9SQ
